mission: Ongoing original and copyright-respecting competitive research for Bizarre Past, What If in 40 Seconds and Little Wild Adventures. Grow views, engaged views, retention, subscribers and monetization eligibility through stronger content; never replicate third-party scripts/scenes/characters/music.
cadence: Weekly cross-channel research plus micro-research in each channel agent before preparing videos.
confidenceGuidelines: Use dated primary channel videos where possible; label third-party counts as dated estimates.
Compare views at similar video ages and by format; don't confuse correlation with causation.
Separate what we observed from what we propose to test. Never guarantee virality.
Use public watch pages and sources without unnecessary paid vidIQ calls; never buy credits automatically.
Use YT Analytics / Metricool for our channel performance, where available.
Made-for-kids videos often disable comments; do not interact with children's content to game engagement.

whatifIdeas.workingTitle: What If Flowers Sent Invisible Electric Messages? ⚡🌼
whatifIdeas.shortHook: What if flowers sent electric messages you could never see?
whatifIdeas.length: 35–40 sec vertical Short, subject to quality/editing; not generated or booked
notDuplicateOf: What If the Ocean Glowed Like Stars?
What If Octopuses Lived on Land?
whatifIdeas.scienceVerified: Bumblebees (Bombus terrestris) can sense and distinguish weak floral electric fields. Charged bee visits briefly alter the flower's potential; electric information alongside color helps learning. The degree to which field changes signal depleted rewards in nature is suggested, not a guaranteed real-time 'closed' signal. Invisible 'glow' must be labelled conceptual animation, not actual light.
whatifIdeas.scriptDraft: What if flowers sent electric messages you could never see? Bumblebees can pick up tiny electrical clues around flowers. As a bee flies, it carries an electric charge, while flowers have weak electric fields. When a bee lands, those fields can change. Scientists discovered bumblebees can learn different electrical patterns and use them together with flower colors to find rewards. So a garden isn't only filled with beautiful colors and sweet scents. For a bumblebee, there's a hidden electrical world too!
whatifIdeas.storyboard: 0–2s strong floral macro + animated translucent contour line (scientific visualization only). 2–10s ordinary flower vs overlay of field as a diagram; 10–19s bee flies, contact, subtle waveform shift; 19–29s illustration of experimental contrasting flower signals and honeybee choosing; 29–40s wide bright garden reveal + key conclusion. Distinguish animation from actual observation in caption; no supernatural glowing flowers.
alternatives: What if flowers had a secret sense just for bees?
What if a garden was full of electrical clues?
What if bees could sense messages hidden in flowers?
What if every flower had an invisible electrical fingerprint?
What if flowers sent electric messages you could never see?
whatifIdeas.creativeQC: Current mixed visual What If style acceptable: documentary stock macro, tasteful simple schematic overlay, short original animated moment if cost-effective, real voice and music. Must start spoken and written 'What if' in first 0–2s and title on-screen ~2–3s; finish complete payoff; not all scenes full motion.
whatifIdeas.experiment: Compare viewer stays-to-watch / engaged views and retention at 24 hours and 7 days with What If's other 35–40s science/nature Shorts of matched age. If credible, evaluate same theme for 3–4 min long form without reusing identical script.
whatifIdeas.publicationBlock: What If AutoPilot recurring timing and unique-slot queue still unverified. DO NOT publish or schedule agent video yet. Need explicit confirmation there is no concurrent AutoPilot publish.

whatifIdeas.scienceVerified: Moonbows really exist: bright nearly full Moon low on horizon plus water droplets opposite Moon in dark sky. Usually appear pale or white to human eyes, while long-exposure photos show more color. Not every night, not glowing neon to naked eye.
